schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme (16 pages). PDF 9 Léamhthuiscint A and B (each question’s asks restated with one price for the question, the two 0–5 language deductions and the penalty note; no answers); 10 Prós Ainmnithe (2A: Hurlamaboc and Oisín i dTír na nÓg reprinted, each with its point prices) and Prós Roghnach (2B: (a) and (b) reprinted with their prices); 11 Filíocht Ainmnithe (a) Géibheann (reprinted with the poem); 12 (b) An tEarrach Thiar (its (i) price cut at the right margin, “(8 mar”) and the examiner’s note; 13 Filíocht Roghnach (3B) and the examiner’s note; 14 Socruithe Réasúnta. PDF 1–8 belong to Paper 1; 15–16 are empty.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1–3 cover and instructions, 4–7 the two reading passages, 8–11 literature, 12 blank) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page (scheme PDF 9–13 rendered; PDF 12’s “(8 mar” confirmed on the render); each prompt and scheme slice is asserted against the PDFs by the builder, which also asserts that the Paper 2 scheme pages print no sample answer, answer bullet or band table.

nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required. The scheme prints no answers: it restates what each question asks and prices the whole question at 10 (the paper prints “10 marc” per question and no price per part). Each question is one card with one 10-mark criterion (the restatement line), claimed whole at 0/10: a split between (a) and (b) would be a price the SEC never printed, so no part is a practice card of its own. The card says “The scheme prints no answer for this part.”

Reading language: “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh.]” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a question. The penalty note (iomarcaíocht) is the examiner’s, carried in no guidance.

Prescribed prose (2A, both answered): (a) Hurlamaboc, a summary covering six printed points, priced “6 phointe eolais. ( 5 mharc ar an gcéad phointe + 5 phointe eile ar 4 mharc an ceann).”: one 25-mark criterion that steps one point at a time (0, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25). The scheme prices the first point made and the rest, not each printed point, so no point is a practice card at a price of its own. (b) Oisín i dTír na nÓg, “4 phointe eolais. (7 marc ar an gcéad phointe + 6 mharc an ceann ar trí phointe eile).”: 0, 7, 13, 19, 25.

Optional prose (2B, both answered): (a) an extract from a novel (an account of the main character, 23) and (b) a folk tale (an account of the main events, 23), each with its title line (2: the novel’s title and author, the tale’s title). Each price is printed whole with no points, scale or samples, so each criterion is claimed whole (0/23, 0/2). No film or play is offered in 2012.

Prescribed poetry (3A, both answered): (a) Géibheann and (b) An tEarrach Thiar, each (i) four printed questions (a)–(d) priced together at 8, (ii) 8 and (iii) 9; each sub-question is its own criterion and practice card, claimed whole (no split, scale or sample is printed). (i)(a)–(d) are not separate cards: the scheme prices them only together.

Optional poetry (3B, both answered): (a) a modern poem by a woman and (b) a modern poem by a man, each (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 7 and the title and poet 2, each claimed whole; the poem itself is open content chosen inside one route.

Choice is not a route: every printed question is one card carrying the printed choice and “Freagair (a) agus (b) anseo.”; no combination cards. The 0–4 Gaeilge deduction is one criterion per literature card, applied once.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 reading 100 (A Evanne Ní Chuilinn: Guth Úr Nua i Roinn Spóirt RTÉ 50, B Dáithí Ó hEithir: Laoch Óg Leadóige 50; five questions at 10 each), Ceist 2 prose 50 (A: (a) Hurlamaboc 25 + (b) Oisín i dTír na nÓg 25; or B: (a) a novel extract 25 + (b) a folk tale 25), Ceist 3 poetry 50 (A: (a) Géibheann 25 + (b) An tEarrach Thiar 25; or B: (a) 25 + (b) 25).

Printed asks: reading 19 (A 1(a), 1(b), 2(a), 2(b), 3(a), 3(b), 4, 5(a), 5(b); B 1(a)–5(b)); literature 31 (2A(a) six points, 2A(b) 1, 2B(a) account + title 2, 2B(b) 2, each 3A poem’s (i)(a)–(d), (ii) and (iii) 12, 3B(a) and 3B(b) (i), (ii), (iii) and title 8).
The Paper 2 scheme prints no sample answers, answer bullets or band tables: only the reading restatements and prices, the literature reprints with prices, and 2A’s two point-price notes.

Scheme misprints kept as printed: Reading A’s restatement names “Evanne Ní Choileáin” (passage: Ní Chuilinn) and “Kieran Boland” (passage: Behan), and writes “faoin a cuid oibre” and “Bh Á C”; B 2’s price reads “= 10 mar”; PDF 12 cuts 3A(b)(i)’s price at the right margin (“(8 mar”), so that criterion’s guidance is the paper’s own print of (i) with “(8 marc)” (paper page 10).
Paper misprints kept as printed: Reading A 5(b) “Cén fath” (for “fáth”); B 2’s price “10marc” (no space).
